message.content:
I don’t have a database of individual security guards, but I can point you toward the best ways to find a highly‑rated professional in New York: | What you’re looking for | How to find it | Tips | |--------------------------|----------------|------| | **Private security guard** | • Search “private security guard services New York” on Google or Bing.
• Check local business directories (Yelp, Yellow Pages, Manta).
• Look at industry sites such as the National Association of Security Companies (NASCO) or the International Association of Professional Security Consultants (IAPSC). | • Read reviews and ratings; look for consistent 4‑5 star feedback.
• Verify that the guard holds a valid NY State security license (issued by the NYS Department of State). | | **Security guard agencies** | • Use the NYS Department of State’s “Licensed Security Guard Agencies” search tool.
• Browse the “New York City Police Department – Private Security” list for approved vendors.
• Check the Better Business Bureau (BBB) for accredited agencies. | • Ask for references and check their track record (e.g., number of incidents handled, client testimonials). | | **Specialized expertise** | • If you need a guard with specific skills (e.g., crowd control, armed escort, cyber‑security liaison), add those keywords to your search.
• Contact local trade associations (e.g., New York State Association of Security Professionals). | • Confirm certifications such as Certified Protection Professional (CPP) or Physical Security Professional (PSP). | | **Cost & availability** | • Request quotes from at least 3–5 providers.
• Ask about scheduling flexibility (24/7 coverage, shift patterns). | • Compare rates, but remember that the lowest price isn’t always the best quality. | ### Quick Steps to Take Now 1. **Search online**: - Google: *“top rated security guard New York”* - Yelp: filter by rating and read recent reviews. 2. **Check licensing**: - Visit the NYS Department of State website and use the “License Lookup” tool to confirm the guard or agency’s license status. 3. **Ask for references**: - A reputable guard will provide references from past clients or employers. Call them to verify performance. 4. **Interview**: - Discuss training, emergency protocols, and how they handle conflict resolution. A good guard will explain procedures clearly. 5. **Get a written agreement**: - Ensure the contract covers scope of work, hours, pay, insurance, and liability clauses. --- If you have a particular type of guard in mind (e.g., armed vs. unarmed, event security vs. corporate office security), let me know and I can tailor the search tips even more closely to your needs.
